subject: Pilot: burst & latency targets — intake and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Erin Jacobs <erin@loopwear.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + asks: pilot targets & sample payloads

Erin — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and immediate asks so we can spin up a scoped pilot next week.

Summary (from today's discovery):
- Goal: validate Loopwear search/recommendation backend on Redwood hosted inference with production-like traffic for 4 weeks, then evaluate cost/latency and success criteria for GA decision.
- Primary model workload: short-form product descriptions -> category & attributes. Avg tokens ~220, 90th perc ~520; some long-form queries up to ~2,200 tokens for multi-product prompts.
- Key SLA ask: 95th percentile generation latency < 500ms for 2k token payloads during steady state; tolerate up to 1.5s under short bursts.

Immediate asks (please reply with values or artifacts):
1) Typical steady-state RPS and expected concurrency during business hours (example: 80 rps sustained between 09:00-17:00 UTC, concurrency ≈ 60).
2) Burst profile: peak RPS and typical burst duration (e.g., 10 min peak at 600 rps after batch ingest).
3) Representative payloads / sample requests (we requested a small sample file during the call).
4) Any PII or retention restrictions (we discussed only product metadata, confirm none of the payloads include customer PII).

Proposed quick pilot plan (subject to your confirmation):
- Week 0: exchange sample payloads + whitelist egress CIDRs; Redwood prepares pilot env and staging API keys.
- Week 1: smoke run (small-scale) to validate integration and tokenization; measure latency baseline.
- Weeks 2–3: ramp to target steady-state RPS and run 48–72h burst tests; capture token-level cost and perf.
- Week 4: readout and recommendation (quantized model variants, batching parameters, caching strategy).

Success criteria (candidate):
- Functional: 95% match to current label accuracy on a holdout eval set (we'll ask for a small eval set).
- Latency: 95th <= 500ms for 2k-token requests under steady-state traffic.
- Cost: projected per-1M tokens cost in line with your target (we'll estimate once we have sample tokenization distribution).

Attachments: [Attachment: poc_checklist_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 78KB)]

Next steps: Erin — can you send the sample_requests.jsonl (up to 5k requests) and confirm burst numbers by EOD tomorrow? I'll copy in Vivek and Laura to line up resources.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Erin Jacobs <erin@loopwear.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael@loopwear.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + asks: pilot targets & sample payloads

Thanks Ben — good call. Details below and I've attached a sample.

Quick numbers (prod last 30 days):
- Steady-state: 45 rps average across region (US east), with concurrency ~28 on our API gateway.
- Peak bursts: up to 720 rps during marketing pushes; typical burst profile is 3–7 minutes at peak, sometimes 20–30 minutes with taper.
- Token lengths: median 210, mean 275, 95th 1,050, tail up to ~2,400 tokens (rare product bundle queries).
- SLO expectation: 95th generation latency < 600ms ideally; we can accept up to 1s for protected maintenance windows.

Attachments: [Attachment: loopwear_sample_requests.jsonl (jsonl, 1.2MB)] — includes 3,000 anonymized request rows, token counts, and a small labeled eval set (250 examples). No customer PII in the file.

We can also provide a short-lived test key and a list of egress IPs once we finalize the NDA/SOW.

One open Q from our side: how does Redwood handle prefix caching when the same user polls repeatedly during the 30s polling window? We want to ensure cache hit behavior doesn't skew latency metrics.

Erin Jacobs
Lead ML Engineer, Loopwear
erin@loopwear.com | +1 617-555-0126

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + asks: pilot targets & sample payloads

Erin — thanks for the fast turnaround and the sample file. That is exactly what we need to size the pilot. Couple of clarifications and our commitments below.

Clarifications from Redwood:
- Prefix/KV caching: Redwood will not artificially conflate cache hits across different user identifiers. For the pilot we will run in a mode that logs cache-hit rates and exposes a flag to disable prefix-level caching so we can measure uncached latencies. If you prefer, we can run two short windows (cached vs uncached) during the burst test.
- Burst simulation: based on your profile we recommend two burst modes during pilot: short sharp (5–7 min at 700–750 rps) and long taper (20–30 min peaking 500–600 rps). We'll orchestrate both.

POC ownership (Redwood side):
- SE lead: Laura Bennett (laura.bennett@redwood.com) — integration, smoke test, baseline tuning.
- CSM: Monica Patel (monica.patel@redwood.com) — timeline coordination and success criteria signoff.
- Infra lead: Vivek Kulkarni — capacity and performance diagnostics.

Confirmed pilot acceptance criteria (please confirm or propose edits):
1) Functional: model responses meet the sample eval set pass rate >= 94% (we'll roll up per-class metrics).
2) Latency: under steady-state simulated traffic, 95th <= 600ms for requests with token_count <= 2,000.
3) Burst tolerance: during short bursts (<=10 mins) 95th <= 1.2s; for long taper bursts 95th <= 1.5s.
4) Observability: access to token-level logs, per-request trace ids, and aggregated cost estimates for the run.

Pilot timeline (target):
- Today (Nov 4): we ingest the sample file and pre-tokenize to produce a token distribution report.
- Nov 6: staging API key + egress CIDRs shared by Loopwear; Redwood returns smoke-run checklist.
- Nov 9: smoke test (integration + short cached/uncached runs).
- Nov 10–16: steady-state ramp + burst windows.
- Nov 20: readout and optimization recommendations.

Action items for Loopwear (please confirm by Nov 6):
- Provide staging API endpoint and a test key with limited scope OR confirm Redwood can call a staging endpoint behind your gateway.
- Provide egress CIDR ranges (for firewall allowlist).
- Confirm the labeled eval set is acceptable for the functional criteria.

Related links: staging checklist and template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/345678

I'll mark Laura & Monica for the operational handoff — Laura, please schedule the smoke run and confirm the runbook items below.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni | Infra Lead
Redwood Inference
